title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Greenville, SC: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Upstate gas turbine, automotive, aerospace and plant construction welding inspectors: Part C choice, Part B travel, eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Greenville: Six Days for Upstate Turbine, Automotive, Aerospace and Construction Welding Inspectors
html:
The Upstate of South Carolina is in the middle of a manufacturing build-out. GE Vernova is installing more than 500 pieces of new equipment at its Greenville gas turbine plant and plans to triple turbine output there to 80 units a year, according to a December 2025 SC Daily Gazette report. BMW opened its Woodruff high-voltage battery plant in November 2026 to feed Plant Spartanburg, which now builds the iX5, the first fully electric BMW assembled in the United States. And Lockheed Martin's Greenville site is, in the company's words, the world's only active F-16 production line. Each of those projects brings new buildings, new equipment and new suppliers, and every one of them leans on people who can judge a weld against a written standard.

Atlantis NDT offers a six-day preparation course for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination for welders, pipefitters, maintenance technicians, QC inspectors, NDT technicians and engineers across Greenville, Spartanburg, Anderson and the rest of the Upstate. AWS, the American Welding Society, sets and runs the examination and is the body that issues the certification. Each candidate applies to AWS individually and has to satisfy its education, experience and vision rules personally. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has never had access to AWS examination content. There is no Atlantis classroom in Greenville. The six days can be taken online at your own pace, delivered for a group at your employer's site, or booked one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed when you book. The topics for each day are set out on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

The Upstate's manufacturing boom, project by project

Employer and siteWhat has been reportedWhere welding inspection comes in
GE Vernova, Greenville gas turbine plantPlans to triple output to 80 turbines a year, install more than 500 pieces of new equipment and hire 650 people; more than 2,500 South Carolina workers; a plant of about 1.55 million square feet (SC Daily Gazette, December 2025)Plant expansion steel, equipment supports, utility and process piping, and component suppliers working to the manufacturer's specifications
BMW Plant Spartanburg and Plant WoodruffWoodruff began series production of Gen6 batteries in November 2026 for vehicles assembled at Spartanburg, which BMW calls the largest plant in its global network and which is slated to assemble at least six fully electric models by 2030Construction and retooling of production halls, conveyors and fixtures, and the supplier base that builds tooling and welded assemblies
Lockheed Martin, GreenvilleIn December 2025 the company completed the initial F-16 Block 70 fleets for Bulgaria and Slovakia at what it describes as the only active F-16 line in the worldAerospace suppliers that fusion weld parts to aerospace specifications, plus tooling and ground equipment

Read the table as a map of where work is coming from, not as a hiring forecast. Plans change, and the welding on a project often belongs to contractors and suppliers rather than to the name on the sign.

Where a CWI fits in a turbine plant expansion

A gas turbine factory is mostly machining, assembly and test, but tripling output means building and installing a great deal of steel. New equipment needs foundations, anchor plates, frames and platforms; test cells need fuel, oil and cooling piping; cranes and lifting fixtures need supports. That construction work is typically welded to AWS D1.1 for structural steel and to ASME piping rules for pressure systems, and project specifications frequently make a CWI responsible for weld inspection. The SC Daily Gazette reported that the plant recruits heavily from Greenville's technical college, which tells you where much of the local welding talent comes from.

Turbine components themselves are a different matter. Welding on a manufactured part follows the manufacturer's own engineering specifications and qualification rules, and those documents decide who may inspect. A CWI is respected background in that setting, but the customer's specification governs.

Source inspection is a growing share of Upstate weld inspection. When an expansion brings in fabricated skids, pipe spools, platforms and tanks from shops across the Southeast, the owner or the contractor often sends an inspector to the fabricator before anything ships. The job is to compare what was built with the drawings and the purchase order: mill certificates against heat numbers, welder and procedure qualification records against the joints actually made, weld sizes and profiles against the drawing, and repairs against the approved repair method. Finding a missing fillet or an unqualified welder in the vendor's shop costs far less than finding it after installation, and the CWI's grounding in symbols, procedure records and visual acceptance criteria is what the role calls for.

Car plants weld differently

An inspector who moves from construction into automotive quickly learns that most body-in-white joining is resistance spot welding, adhesive bonding and other high-volume processes checked by teardown, sampling and in-line monitoring rather than by gauge-in-hand visual inspection. BMW's Woodruff release describes battery cell clusters and contact systems that are laser-cleaned and welded, with every weld seam inspected in line. None of that is the subject of the CWI exam.

Where the CWI matters in the automotive cluster is everywhere around the car: the construction steel for new halls, conveyor structures, welded fixtures and tooling, maintenance repairs on presses and robots, and the tier suppliers that weld brackets, frames and assemblies to customer drawings. A supplier quality team that can show a certified welding inspector reviewed its procedures and signed off its first articles has an easier time with customer audits.

Aerospace suppliers and the D17.1 option

Most airframe structure is fastened rather than welded, but aerospace supply chains still include fusion-welded parts such as ducts, brackets, engine components, tooling and ground support equipment. For those, AWS offers AWS D17.1, the specification for fusion welding for aerospace applications, as a Part C choice in its 2024 edition. A candidate who spends most of the week on aerospace weldments should look at D17.1, while one who also handles plant steel and fixtures may be better served by D1.1. Aerospace customers generally flow down their own requirements for who may inspect, so check what your customer's specification expects before assuming the CWI covers it. For NDT on aerospace parts, see aerospace NDT training.

Choosing a Part C book for Upstate work

Part C is open book, between 50 and 65 questions on the code you choose. The AWS CWI page in November 2026 listed these options and editions, matched here to common Upstate jobs:

If most of your work isConsider
Building steel, equipment supports, conveyors, fixtures and general fabricationAWS D1.1, 2020 edition
Process, steam, fuel and cooling piping in plants and test facilitiesASME Section IX (2023) with B31.1 and B31.3 (2024)
Fusion-welded aerospace parts and aerospace toolingAWS D17.1, 2024 edition
Bridge fabrication and repair for state and local agenciesAWS D1.5, 2020 edition including Clause 12
Aluminum structuresAWS D1.2, 2014 edition
Gas transmission and distribution pipelinesAPI 1104, 22nd edition

The exam edition can be older than the copy in your quality office, and clause and table numbers do move between editions, so study the edition AWS lists. More reading: AWS D1.1, ASME Section IX, ASME B31.3 and AWS D1.5.

I-85 and the bridge work a study could lead to

Interstate work along the I-85 corridor is still at the planning stage. In December 2025 SCDOT announced a 2026 study of I-85 from US 29 (Exit 34) to SC 85 (Exit 69), about 35 miles with 18 interchanges through the Anderson, Greenville and Spartanburg area, and described it as a planning-level effort that could lead to later improvements. No construction commitment follows from a study, but when interchanges of that kind are rebuilt, steel bridge girders and their attachments are normally fabricated to AWS D1.5 under the agency's specifications. An inspector who expects to work for a bridge fabricator or a consultant inspecting fabrication should weigh D1.5 seriously for Part C.

Greenville Technical College and the Western Carolina Section

Greenville Technical College teaches welding at its Brashier Campus, home to its 44,000-square-foot Center for Welding and Automation Excellence. The college offers a Welding and Robotic Technology Certificate in Applied Science, aimed at fabrication shops, maintenance welding and construction pipe welding, and a Specialized Welding certificate covering plate, mild steel pipe and stainless steel pipe with gas metal arc and gas tungsten arc welding. Its program description lists blueprint reading, weld quality evaluation, pipe fitting and preparation for industry welder testing. Those subjects are a good foundation for the CWI, and graduates generally apply under the trade or vocational line of the AWS experience table, subject to AWS review.

The AWS Western Carolina Section, part of District 8, is active in Greenville. In January 2026 it held a joint AWS and ASME professional development meeting at the Greenville Technical College Student Success Center on why properly qualified welding procedures sometimes still produce poor welds, with a focus on corrosion-resistant alloys. Meetings like that are useful before the exam and after it, because professional development hours are one of the routes AWS accepts at nine-year recertification.

Kennesaw is the usual Part B trip

Parts A and C are computer-based and taken at a Prometric test center after AWS accepts your application. Part B is held at AWS seminar locations, usually on the Saturday or Sunday after a three-day Part B seminar at the same place, and the AWS list of CWI training locations includes no site in South Carolina. Kennesaw, Georgia, is the listed site most Upstate candidates will look at first, with Birmingham, Alabama, and Norfolk, Virginia, as the other options in the region. For US exams that include Part B, AWS wants the application six weeks before the Part B date, and each part needs a minimum score of 72 percent.

The Part B paper has 46 questions tied to hands-on work with specimens, gauges and documents AWS hands out, including applying a procedure specification and its qualification record to what you see. Practise measuring fillet size, convexity, undercut depth and misalignment on real welds until the numbers come quickly and consistently. For the travel budget, try the CWI exam cost calculator.

Which line of the experience table are you on?

AWS weighs schooling against welding-related work experience. On the AWS CWI page, a bachelor's degree or higher in welding engineering or technology means one year of experience; an associate degree or higher in welding or a related engineering technology, engineering or a physical science, two years; engineering or technical courses applicable to a welding bachelor's degree, three; completed trade or vocational courses, four; a high school diploma or equivalent, five; eighth-grade schooling, nine; and less than eighth grade, twelve. For Upstate candidates, a few common starting points:

  • Technical college welding certificate: usually the four-year line, if AWS accepts the program. Keep your transcript with the application.
  • Engineering degree, working in plant engineering or supplier quality: the two-year line, documented through the procedures, inspection plans, first-article reports and weld rejections you handled.
  • High school diploma and years on construction or maintenance crews: the five-year line, which depends on every employer confirming dates and welding duties.
  • NDT technician certified by an employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A: AWS decides whether the inspection years count as welding-related, so describe the weld examination duties precisely.

Whatever the line, you must also pass the AWS vision test, recorded on the AWS visual acuity form, recent enough to be current at exam time. More detail in the CWI requirements guide.

Running the six days for an Upstate contractor or plant

A construction contractor, fabricator or plant with several candidates can have the six days delivered at its yard or facility. The group works with its own weld samples and gauges, and the Part C sessions follow the book most of them will choose, usually D1.1 for structural contractors and the ASME package for piping contractors. Upstate employers often time the course before a large expansion job or a new supply contract, so that qualified inspectors are already in place when the work arrives. Every member of the group still submits an individual AWS application with personal experience evidence and a current vision record. Individual candidates who work long weeks on expansion projects often prefer the online format, which has no scheduled class times and lets them send written questions to the instructor between shifts.

After the CWI

Under AWS rules the certification lasts nine years, with renewal applications at the third and sixth years. At nine years, AWS lists recertification by retaking Part B, by 80 professional development hours, through the Certified Radiographic Interpreter credential, through an endorsement exam passed before the ninth year, through the Senior CWI exams or through the nine-year course. Many Upstate inspectors also add NDT methods, which the employer certifies under its written practice; Atlantis provides training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, including VT Level 2, PT Level 2, MT Level 2 and UT Level 2. Local pages: NDT training in Greenville and ultrasonic testing in Greenville. CWI exam prep elsewhere in the Southeast: Charlotte, Atlanta and North Charleston.

Contacting Atlantis from the Upstate

Tell us the format you want, how many people are involved, the Part C book each expects to choose and the period in which they hope to sit the exam. For a group at your site, name the weeks that clash with commissioning, shutdowns or a product launch. If an experience record looks borderline, describe it and we will say what to confirm with AWS before applying. Fees for every format are quoted on request, and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Greenville?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Greenville. You study online at your own pace, as part of a group at your employer's site, or one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed when you book. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad.

faq.q: Can I take Part B in South Carolina?
faq.a: The AWS list of CWI training locations has no South Carolina site. Kennesaw, Georgia, is the listed site most Upstate candidates use, and Birmingham and Norfolk are the other regional options.

faq.q: Which Part C book suits construction work at a turbine or auto plant expansion?
faq.a: AWS D1.1 for structural steel, supports and fixtures, or the ASME package of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3 if your work is mainly plant piping.

faq.q: I work for an aerospace supplier. Should I take D17.1?
faq.a: If most of your welding inspection is on fusion-welded aerospace parts, AWS D17.1 is the natural choice. If you also inspect plant steel and fixtures, compare it with D1.1, and check what your customer's specification requires of inspectors.

faq.q: Does a CWI help with resistance spot welds in a car plant?
faq.a: Only indirectly. High-volume automotive joining is checked by teardown, sampling and in-line monitoring under the manufacturer's standards. The CWI is most useful in plant construction, tooling, maintenance and supplier fabrication.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Greenville?
faq.a: Yes. The AWS Western Carolina Section, in District 8, held a joint AWS and ASME professional development meeting at Greenville Technical College in January 2026. The section finder on aws.org lists upcoming meetings.

faq.q: I finished a Greenville Tech welding certificate. How much experience do I need?
faq.a: Completed trade or vocational courses put you on the four-year line of the AWS table, as long as AWS accepts the program and your work as welding-related. A high school diploma alone calls for five years.

faq.q: Has AWS endorsed the Atlantis CWI course?
faq.a: No. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has no view of AWS examination content or results. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: How do I request a quote from Greenville?
faq.a: Give us the format, the head count and each person's Part C book using the enquiry link here. We quote each format on request and reply within one business day.
